title: Pawn races and the square

D0.outcome: Says that a pawn needs one move per rank to reach the last rank (two squares allowed on its first move) and that an enemy king may catch it.

D1.outcome: Decides whether a lone king can catch a running pawn by counting the pawn's moves and the king's moves.

D2.outcome: Decides who wins a race when both sides have a pawn about to run, counting moves and noting who is to move and whether the first new queen gives check.

D3.outcome: Checks a race count against the finer points: promotion with check, capturing the other pawn on the way, a king that steps in front.

misconceptions: A king can never catch up with a pawn that has a head start.
Forgetting the pawn's two-square first move when counting.
The king must walk straight at the pawn; the diagonal route costs nothing less.
conditions: Count the pawn's moves to the last rank (two squares allowed on its first move) and the king's moves to the queening square; the side to move gets the first of those moves.
The result of a race is checked with the tablebase when all pieces fit (7 or fewer).
contrasts: A pawn with a head start is still caught when the king is inside its square.
A far-away friendly king that cannot help does not change the count.
